risks.title: Weather and Power Outage Demand Volatility
risks.score_rationale: Residential standby generator demand is driven by major power outage events (hurricanes, winter storms, wildfires, grid instability). Mild weather years cause sharp residential sales declines, as Item 1A acknowledges.
risks.summary: Residential generator sales are highly sensitive to power outage frequency and severity; quiet weather years can cause sharp revenue declines.

risks.title: Channel Inventory and Dealer Network
risks.score_rationale: Generac sells through independent dealers and big-box retailers. Channel destocking (as seen 2022-23) and dealer attrition can disconnect shipments from end demand.
risks.summary: Imbalances in dealer and retail channel inventories can amplify demand swings and pressure margins on price discounting.

risks.title: Clean Energy Segment (Storage) Underperformance
risks.score_rationale: The 2021 ecobee and energy storage acquisitions have generated impairment charges and underperformed; California NEM 3.0 transition reshapes economics.
risks.summary: Continued losses or impairments in the clean energy / storage segment could weigh on consolidated earnings and capital allocation credibility.

risks.title: Commodity, Component and Supply Chain Risk
risks.score_rationale: Engines, alternators, copper, steel and semiconductors are key inputs. 2021-22 chip shortages caused major backlogs; tariffs add complexity.
risks.summary: Volatility in component availability and commodity prices can disrupt production schedules and compress gross margin.

risks.title: Product Safety and Recall Risk
risks.score_rationale: Generac executed a major recall of portable generators in 2023 following CPSC engagement, with material warranty and litigation exposure noted in filings.
risks.summary: Product defects, recalls and related personal injury litigation could result in material charges and reputational damage.

risks.title: Competitive and Technology Transition
risks.score_rationale: Increasing competition from Briggs, Kohler, Cummins and battery-storage alternatives; long-term shift from fossil-fueled generators to electrified backup is a structural risk.
risks.summary: Competition from established C&I players and substitution toward battery storage and microgrids could erode share over time.
